audit_findings.title: Post-year-end acquisition debt is inside the current capital structure but absent from FY2025 owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed $1,250.0 million acquisition financing; Stakeholder contributed $125.4 million of revenue and $22.5 million of net income in 1H2026, while pro forma 1H2025 net income was $19.5 million below reported net income; owner-earnings effect unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: The bridge reflects acquisition-related debt, but the FY2025 OE anchor excludes Stakeholder's operations and financing costs; acquired cash earnings would raise OE while interest and maintenance needs would reduce it.
audit_findings.evidence: On January 6, 2026, we used $650.0 million in borrowings from the Commercial Paper Program and $600.0 million from the Securitization Facility to fund the Stakeholder Acquisition.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter mismatch is demonstrated. Because the valuation does not deduct debt from equity value, omitted acquisition interest is not corrected through the bridge. Filed results show that Stakeholder is economically meaningful, but net income cannot substitute for owner earnings and the opposing effects prevent determining direction.
audit_findings.action: Construct full-year pro forma Stakeholder OE using attributable operating cash earnings, cash interest, maintenance capital and tax effects, then rerun all scenarios on a consistent post-acquisition perimeter.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may be unfunded because growth capital was stripped from owner earnings
audit_findings.magnitude: Computed annual reinvestment of $557.5 million at 3% growth, $1,114.9 million at 6% growth and $464.6 million at 2.5% terminal growth, using growth × $3,214.7 million anchor OE ÷ 17.3% RONTA; filed 2025 growth capital was $3,343.5 million
audit_findings.mechanism: Required reinvestment reduces distributable OE in each growth year and terminal value; omitting it allows OE to grow without funding the tangible assets supporting that growth.
audit_findings.evidence: Growth capital expenditures, net of contributions from noncontrolling interests and including contributions to investments in unconsolidated affiliates, were $3,343.5 million and $3,000.4 million for the years ended December 31, 2025 and 2024.
audit_findings.explanation: No reinvestment deduction is shown in the supplied scenario mechanics despite positive growth and a 2.5% terminal rate. The computed charges equal 17.3%, 34.7% and 14.5% of anchor OE, respectively, and terminal value represents roughly half of scenario PV, so the omission is reasonably capable of changing the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Rerun every scenario with an explicit annual reinvestment charge tied to the unchanged growth rates and 17.3% RONTA, including the 2.5% terminal-growth reinvestment.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may disappear when depreciation is added back
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 finance-lease principal of $76.5 million, equal to 2.4% of anchor OE; approximately $5.0 per share of base-case value if the full amount were recurring and omitted
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back finance-lease depreciation without deducting sustaining principal or equivalent replacement capital would overstate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Finance lease costs are included in Depreciation and amortization expense and Interest expense, net in our Consolidated Statements of Operations.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting-path concern remains unresolved, but the identified 2025 amount is small relative to the $3,214.7 million anchor. A full proportional correction would reduce base value by about $5.0 per share and bull value by about $5.9, versus respective market-price shortfalls of $80.57 and $42.95, so it would not change the current conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $76.5 million principal and related leased-asset replacements through maintenance capex; correct OE if absent, but no standalone conclusion-changing rerun is indicated at the filed scale.

audit_findings.title: Common-equity earnings may contain consolidated-basis add-backs belonging to noncontrolling interests
audit_findings.magnitude: Filed 2025 NCI adjustment of $11.4 million plus a $1.9 million gross-to-net maintenance-capex difference; combined $13.3 million equals 0.41% of anchor OE and approximately $0.87 per share of base-case value
audit_findings.mechanism: Consolidated D&A or maintenance-capex adjustments not reduced to TRGP's ownership could inflate OE while shares represent only common shareholders.
audit_findings.evidence: Third party ownership interests in our controlled subsidiaries are presented as noncontrolling interests within the equity section of our Consolidated Balance Sheets, except in the case of undivided interest ownership.
audit_findings.explanation: The possible calculation mismatch is not demonstrated, but the filed current-year ownership adjustments provide a concrete scale. Even treating both identified amounts as omitted corrections produces less than a 0.5% anchor change. Historical NCI gaps do not drive this valuation because it anchors solely to 2025 OE.
audit_findings.action: Document the 2025 attributable reconciliation for D&A, capitalized interest and maintenance capex, confirming that the $11.4 million NCI adjustment and ownership-funded capex were applied.

audit_findings.title: Badlands tariff revenue remains subject to refund and rate reduction
audit_findings.mechanism: A refund would reduce cash OE, and a lower final tariff would reduce normalized future OE and potentially the growth path.
audit_findings.evidence: Targa Badlands filed this initial tariff in FERC Docket No. IS26-24-000 on October 29, 2025, which FERC accepted and suspended subject to refund pending a hearing to determine, among other things, whether the rates Targa Badlands proposed are just and reasonable.
audit_findings.explanation: The refund exposure and rate challenge are existing conditions affecting revenue recognized under the tariff, not merely forward-looking risks. However, the filings supplied do not isolate challenged revenue, a refund reserve or the difference between proposed and supportable rates, so the record cannot establish materiality.
audit_findings.action: Obtain Badlands revenue billed under the challenged tariff, the accounting reserve, shipper claims and a supportable final-rate range; rerun OE and scenarios if the resulting annual adjustment is material.

audit_findings.title: 45Q income may precede cash realization
audit_findings.magnitude: unquantified; the entire filed 2025 other operating income line was $30.3 million, equal to 0.94% of anchor OE and approximately $2.0 per share of base-case value
audit_findings.mechanism: Recognized 45Q income unsupported by current cash-tax reductions or monetization proceeds would require a timing adjustment to OE.
audit_findings.evidence: We recognize realized 45Q tax credits in excess of Targa’s quarterly estimated tax liability as long-term assets until they are monetized or are otherwise realized.
audit_findings.explanation: The exact unmatched 45Q asset build is not disclosed, so the error itself is unresolved. Even using the entire $30.3 million other-operating-income line as a conservative ceiling, the scale is below 1% of anchor OE and would not bridge the $80.57 difference between base value and market price. Because the credits remain realizable assets, delay principally affects timing rather than eliminating value.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile 2025 45Q income to cash-tax offsets, transfers or monetization receipts and defer any unmatched amount in OE; retain the receivable's discounted realization value where supportable.
